In [[mathematics]], a '''hyperelliptic surface''', or '''bi-elliptic surface''', is a minimal [[surface (mathematics)|surface]] whose [[Albanese morphism]] is an [[elliptic fibration]] without singular fibres. Any such surface can be written as the [[quotient group|quotient]] of a [[direct product|product]] of two elliptic curves by a [[finite abelian group]].
Hyperelliptic surfaces form one of the classes of surfaces of [[Kodaira dimension]] 0 in the [[Enriques–Kodaira classification]].

==Invariants==
The Kodaira dimension is 0.{{Clarification needed|date=August 2024}}

==Classification==
Any hyperelliptic surface is a quotient (''E''×''F'')/''G'', where ''E'' = '''C'''/Λ and ''F'' are elliptic curves, and ''G'' is a subgroup of ''F'' ([[Group action (mathematics)|acting]] on ''F'' by translations), which acts on ''E'' not only by translations. There are seven families of hyperelliptic surfaces as in the following table.

Here ω is a [[primitive nth root of unity|primitive cube root]] of 1 and i is a primitive 4th root of 1.

==Quasi hyperelliptic surfaces==

A '''quasi-hyperelliptic surface''' is a surface whose [[canonical divisor]] is numerically equivalent to zero, the [[Albanese variety|Albanese mapping]] maps to an elliptic curve, and all its [[fiber (mathematics)|fiber]]s are [[rational curve|rational]] with a [[cusp (singularity)|cusp]]. They only exist in [[Characteristic (algebra)|characteristics]] 2 or 3. Their second [[Betti number]] is 2, the second [[Chern number]] vanishes, and the [[holomorphic Euler characteristic]] vanishes. They were classified by {{harv|Bombieri|Mumford|1976}}, who found six cases in characteristic 3 (in which case 6''K''= 0) and eight in characteristic 2 (in which case 6''K'' or 4''K'' vanishes).
Any quasi-hyperelliptic surface is a quotient (''E''×''F'')/''G'', where ''E'' is a [[rational curve]] with one cusp, ''F'' is an elliptic curve, and ''G'' is a finite [[group scheme|subgroup scheme]] of ''F'' (acting on ''F'' by translations).
